title: EVIDENCE_EVENT
description: One line of the append-only ledger. Artifacts say what is true; events say what happened, when, at whose hand and at what cost. Without these there is nothing for cost or evaluation to attach to.

prev.description: sha256 of the previous entry, or 64 zeroes at the head. This is what makes the log append-only in fact rather than by convention: rewriting history breaks every link after it.

kind.description: emitted: an artifact entered the store. gate: a deterministic check ran. decision: authority was granted or refused. action: something left the building. intervention: a human stepped in. exception: automation stopped and asked. promotion: knowledge moved up a layer.

actor.description: Workload identity, SPIFFE-format. Never a person's account - see departments/README.md on identity.

artifacts.description: What went in and what came out, by digest.

goal.description: The goal this event serves. Cost with no goal cannot be divided by an outcome.

policy.description: Digest of the policy version that governed this event. A decision that cannot name its policy cannot be audited.

cost.description: What this event consumed. Tokens are telemetry; the business unit is cost per accepted outcome.

request.description: What the model was asked, on the entry for that invocation. Cost says an agent ran; this says what it was told to do and what it was allowed to touch. An entry that invoked a model and cannot produce this is not auditable.

harness.description: Which agent ran it, by HR_HARNESS selector name.

promptDigest.description: sha256 of the exact prompt text. A digest, not the text: enough to prove a claimed prompt is the one that ran, without copying step input into a committed file.

tools.description: The tool grant the invocation ran under, each entry keeping any argument pattern it was granted with. `Bash(hr impact *)` and `Bash` are different grants, and recording the second for the first would overstate the confinement.

deniedTools.description: Tools denied for this invocation. Deny wins over allow, so an audit that reads only the allow list reads the grant too wide.

procedure.description: Path of the procedure the seat was told to follow.

procedureDigest.description: sha256 of that procedure's content, so editing it later cannot silently change what this entry meant.

untrustedInput.description: This invocation's prompt carried externally derived text. Whatever it produced - a signed artifact included - rests on material hr did not author. An evidence chain that cannot tell this apart from first-hand work overstates itself.
